title: California v. Hodari D. (1991)
key_points: Holding: Federally, a person who flees is not seized until he submits or is physically restrained, so items he throws while running are not the fruit of a seizure.
New Jersey: Rejected by State v. Tucker, 136 N.J. 158 (1994): a seizure occurs when police conduct would lead a reasonable person to believe they are not free to leave.
officer_notes: Scenario: A youth runs as you approach and tosses a bag of drugs before you catch him.
Takeaway: In NJ, do not rely on this rule: NJ looks at when a reasonable person would feel not free to leave.
